literal: In the twelfth month, on gengwu day the new moon, Xiuge was made yuyue.
idiomatic: On the gengwu new moon of the twelfth month Xiuge was invested as yuyue.

literal: A great feast for the troops was held.
idiomatic: The court held a great feast for the troops.

literal: In the third year, spring, second month, on bingzi day, he traveled east.
idiomatic: In the third year, on bingzi day of the second spring month, the Emperor traveled east.

literal: On jichou day, he again went to Nanjing.
idiomatic: On jichou day he again went to Nanjing.

literal: In the third month, on yimao day, Prince Han Ba died.
idiomatic: On yimao day in the third month Prince Han Ba died.

literal: On xinyou day, he was buried between the Huang and Tu rivers, and Yongzhou was established.
idiomatic: On xinyou day the prince was buried between the Huang and Tu rivers and Yongzhou was established.

literal: Prince of Qin Han Kuangsi was made Southwest Route pacification commissioner.
idiomatic: Prince of Qin Han Kuangsi was appointed Southwest Route pacification commissioner.

literal: In summer, fifth month, on bingwu day, Han troops at Shangjing rebelled; attempting to install Xiyin by force they failed, spuriously enthroned his son Liulishou, and Shangjing regent Chushi captured him.
idiomatic: On bingwu day in the fifth summer month Han troops at Shangjing rebelled; failing to install Xiyin by force, they spuriously enthroned his son Liulishou, whom Shangjing regent Chushi captured.

literal: In autumn, seventh month, on jiazi day, Liulishou was executed.
idiomatic: On jiazi day in the seventh autumn month Liulishou was put to death.

literal: In winter, tenth month, he went to Puguipo.
idiomatic: In the tenth winter month the Emperor went to Puguipo.

literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai day, Chushi was additionally made co-director of the Department of State Affairs with the rank of co-chancellor under the Gate.
idiomatic: On xinhai day in the eleventh month Chushi was additionally appointed co-director of the Department of State Affairs with the rank of co-chancellor under the Gate.

literal: That month, Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs Guo Xi was made Wuding Army Military Commissioner.
idiomatic: That month Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs Guo Xi was appointed Wuding Army Military Commissioner.

literal: In the twelfth month, Liaoxing Army Military Commissioner Han Derang was made Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liaoxing Army Military Commissioner Han Derang was appointed Southern Court Commissioner of Military Affairs.

literal: Appraisal: In over sixty years since Liao's rise, between the Shendian and Huitong reigns, there was no day with spare time;
idiomatic: Appraisal: In more than sixty years since Liao's founding, from Shendian through Huitong, the court knew no day of rest;

literal: The rulers of Tianlu and Yingli did not end their reigns as ordained;
idiomatic: The Tianlu and Yingli emperors were not permitted to finish their reigns;

literal: Since Baoning, every person hoped for good governance.
idiomatic: From the Baoning era onward, everyone looked for stable rule.

literal: With Jingzong's endowment, employing men without doubt, rewarding faithfulness and punishing surely, it seemed one could accomplish great things with him.
idiomatic: Jingzong had the makings of a capable ruler: he employed men without suspicion and matched reward to merit and punishment to fault, so that great things seemed within reach.

literal: Yet he exhausted the state's strength to aid Hedong; armies were broken and generals killed, without saving them from extinction.
idiomatic: Yet he drained the state's strength to aid Hedong, breaking armies and losing generals without preventing Han's extinction.

literal: Though he took one compensation from Song, the gain did not repay the loss.
idiomatic: Though he won one reckoning from Song, the gains did not offset the losses.

literal: Knowing Kuangsi's offenses, he enumerated them but did not punish;
idiomatic: He knew Kuangsi's guilt, listed his crimes, yet withheld punishment;

literal: He approved Guo Xi's remonstrance, accepted it but did not use it;
idiomatic: He praised Guo Xi's remonstrance, accepted it in word but ignored it in deed;

literal: The monk Zhaomin, by heterodox ways corrupting virtue, was favored with the post of Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: The monk Zhaomin led men astray with heterodox practices, yet was favored with the post of Palace Attendant.

literal: Is this not confused judgment!
idiomatic: Was this not a bewildering way to govern?
